title: Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: physician analogy — command to preach to all does not prove God decreed to free all efficaciously
pass_a_gloss: To finish in a word: as from this, that God wills all physicians according to their strength so to act, to prepare and offer unto any sick man whom they take to cure those things which conduce unto prolonging his life, it is not rightly inferred that God wills not to permit any to be extinguished by force of disease, except from this, that he foresaw the same as a stubborn contemner of the medicine offered: so from this, that God commands the ministers of the Gospel to preach the word (which is the medicine of souls) unto all, and with all might to strive that all and singular be freed from death, it does not follow that God himself decreed to free all from death efficaciously, or did not decree to permit some by their hard-heartedness to rush into perdition, whom unless he had reprobated, he both could and would have softened by his special mercy. In vain therefore from the mandating will of God, which ought to govern human actions, is judgment made concerning the predestinating or reprobating will of God, which determines some effect to be produced by infallible Divine action, or, that denied, not to be produced.
pass_b_english: In a word: from God's will that every physician do his utmost — prepare and offer each patient he takes on whatever helps prolong life — you may not infer that God will let none die of disease unless he foresaw him a stubborn scorner of the offered medicine. So from God's command that Gospel ministers preach the word (the medicine of souls) to all, and strain every nerve that every one be freed from death, it does not follow that God himself decreed to free all from death efficaciously — or that he did not decree to permit some, by their hard hearts, to rush into perdition whom, had he not reprobated them, he both could and would have softened by special mercy. Vain, then, to judge the predestinating or reprobating will — which determines an effect by infallible divine action, or withholds it — from the mandating will that ought to govern human actions.
source_text: Ut verbo absolvam, sicuti ex eo quod Deus vult omnes medicos pro sua virili ea agere, parare et offerre cuilibet aegroto quem curandum suscipiunt, quae ad vitam ejus producendam conducunt, non recte infertur Deum nolle permittere ut vi morbi ullus extinguatur, nisi exinde quod eundem praeviderit ut medicinae oblatae praefractum contemptorem: sic ex eo quod jubet Deus ministros Evangelicos verbum (quod est animorum medicina) omnibus praedicare, et omni ope eniti, ut omnes et singuli a morte liberentur, non sequitur, ipsum Deum decrevisse omnes a morte efficaciter liberare, aut non decrevisse permittere quosdam sua duricordia in perditionem ruere, quos nisi reprobasset, et potuisset et voluisset speciali sua misericordia emollire. Frustra igitur ex voluntate Dei mandante, quae actiones humanas debet gubernare, de voluntate Dei praedestinante aut reprobante judicatur, quae effectum aliquem producendum infallibili actione Divina, aut ea negata non producendum, determinat.
